applePolicy.assessment: Bundling the runtime is not automatic approval, and an unbundled Web/WASM runtime is not automatic prohibition. The release owner must classify the actual delivery route and ensure the final bundle/download behavior satisfies the applicable guideline conditions. The LGPL libraries are inside the WASM, not the signed native App binary; LGPL obligations attach to the WASM distribution regardless of WebKit. This profile does not claim App Store approval, legal clearance or acceptance. Apple code signing/DRM does not by itself satisfy LGPL relink; the source + build/relink or source/build-tool-only route preserves the required freedom.
applePolicy.guideline2_5_2_summary: The guidelines expect an app bundle to be self-contained and restrict downloading, installing or executing code that introduces or changes app features; a limited educational exception exists. Whether the Floe IDE/developer flow falls within that exception is not established by this source profile.
applePolicy.guideline4_7_summary: The guidelines separately describe HTML5/JavaScript mini apps and mini games that are not embedded in the binary, and make the developer responsible for that software and its compliance with the applicable conditions.
applePolicy.releaseOwnerAction: Decide bundled vs downloaded runtime delivery, classify the Floe IDE/developer flow, and confirm the applicable guideline conditions; do not treat this assessment as approval.

obligations.lgplMethod: LGPL-2.1 section 6(a): complete corresponding source + the work that uses the Library in source form so the user can modify the library and relink
obligations.noDynamicLoophole: The WASM statically embeds the LGPL objects; Floe does not rely on a shared-library exception.
obligations.noticeDelivery: Each prepared resource carries the full notice bundle; source packages are in the release source depot.
obligations.reverseEngineering: No Floe restriction; users may modify and relink for debugging their modifications.
obligations.writtenOfferFallback: If the release cannot publish source with the binary, include the LGPL 2.1 section 6(c) written offer valid at least three years.
